generated_note: Curated projection of docs/history/experiment_timeline.md and docs/ADAPTIVERAG_REPORT.md. Committed so the Research Journey page renders on a fresh clone.

phases.name: Corpus Foundation
phases.hypothesis: 14 foundational IR/NLP papers suffice to compare retrieval strategies meaningfully.
phases.experiment: Deterministic download, PDF magic-byte and SHA-256 validation, metadata manifest.
phases.decision: Proceed; raw PDFs kept out of git, reproducible via script.

phases.name: Dense RAG Baseline
phases.objective: The fixed Dense-RAG baseline everything else is measured against.
phases.hypothesis: A bi-encoder over structure-aware chunks gives a strong single-stage baseline.
phases.experiment: Ingestion, structure-aware chunking, embedding, Qdrant, retrieval, evaluation on the 20-query set.
phases.result: Dense Recall@5 0.8417, MRR 0.95, ~750 ms (dominated by the embedding API call).
phases.decision: Adopt as the quality reference and the expensive rung.

phases.name: BM25 Lexical Baseline
phases.objective: An independent cheap strategy over the same corpus.
phases.hypothesis: Lexical retrieval is dramatically cheaper and modestly worse.
phases.result: BM25 Recall@5 0.7167, MRR 0.6771, 1.48 ms (~500x cheaper than Dense).
phases.decision: Keep as the cheap rung and the no-API latency control arm.

phases.name: Hybrid Retrieval (RRF)
phases.objective: Does rank fusion of the two beat either?
phases.hypothesis: RRF(dense, BM25) recovers evidence each misses.
phases.experiment: RRF fusion, k=20 per arm, top-10 out.
phases.result: Hybrid Recall@5 0.8583 - better than BM25, below Dense. Fusion flattens ranked scores.
phases.decision: Keep as a selectable strategy; note that Dense alone leads.

phases.name: Reranking (cross-encoder)
phases.objective: Does a cross-encoder second stage pay for itself?
phases.hypothesis: Reranking the top-N lifts precision at acceptable cost.
phases.experiment: ONNX cross-encoder over all three first-stages + candidate-depth ablation.
phases.result: Every head metric fell (MRR -0.083 / -0.061 / -0.127); depth ablation makes R@5 fall as latency climbs; ~155 ms per candidate pair.
phases.decision: Record as observed; the rung is not adopted as a default.

phases.name: Adaptive Routing (orchestration layer)
phases.objective: A query-aware decision layer over the unchanged strategies.
phases.hypothesis: Deterministic query features plus a label-free sufficiency check can pick a strategy and escalate when warranted.
phases.result: Implemented and validated; the sufficiency gate never fires at the shipped defaults, so adaptive collapses onto its initial pick.

phases.name: Evaluation & Ablations
phases.objective: Does adaptive routing earn its complexity?
phases.hypothesis: Adaptive beats fixed strategies on the quality/cost frontier.
phases.experiment: E1 five-arm comparison (107 queries), E2 escalation ablation, E3 feature ablation, E4 threshold sweep, E5 cost-weight sweep; then two pre-registered closure gates.
phases.result: Adaptive = hybrid on quality at ~59 ms overhead; E2 shows escalation buys latency not quality; 0/24 feature hits; the gate never opens at 0.3-0.6. Gate 2: oracle headroom +0.0218/+0.0343 on only 4-6/107 queries. Gate 3: OOS AUC 0.534, 0/24 Holm.
phases.decision: Close Phase 7 with a bounded negative answer: headroom exists, is not identifiable out of sample, and a router is not established.

phases.name: Corpus Fix Study (before/after)
phases.objective: Was the corpus defect responsible for the reranker collapse and for 'dense dominates hybrid'?
phases.hypothesis: A diagnosed two-column extraction defect explains both.
phases.experiment: Fix extraction, re-chunk/re-embed, re-run all five arms on a before and after corpus; plus a gold-label audit and a run-integrity re-sweep.
phases.result: Quality unchanged on every arm; reranker -0.0016 (99/107 ties); both rescue outcomes excluded; 47 of 140 section labels corrupt (22 repairable); 13 of 29 arms in the first sweep were silently invalid.
phases.decision: Withdraw the corpus attribution (the recommendation to drop the rung stands, its rationale does not); exclude nDCG@5; keep the cost table unfrozen (recommendation: do not freeze).

phases.name: Signal Discovery
phases.objective: Which measurable properties explain per-query dispersion, and is any of them known in advance?
phases.hypothesis: Dispersion across strategies is real and partly predictable.
phases.experiment: 12-hypothesis family (Holm denominator 12) screened against T-disp3 on both arms; five gates.
phases.result: Dispersion is real (21/29 of 107). Dense distinct-document ratio tracks it (rho +0.343/+0.406, OOS +0.410) and generalizes. No query-only pre-routing signal exists (best abs(rho) = 0.194).
phases.decision: Build no router under any verdict; justify testing a two-stage post-dense decision next (Phase 10).

phases.name: Post-Dense Escalation
phases.objective: Can DDR decide whether Dense to Hybrid escalation is worth it?
phases.hypothesis: The dispersion signal predicts escalation gain.
phases.experiment: Frozen oracle and threshold, one-pass test on both arms, with a random-at-equal-rate ablation.
phases.result: AUC 0.550 (chance); test delta -0.050 / -0.033 vs dense-only; TP 0/2 per arm; random beats the policy (P = 1.000 / 0.954). Escalation helps 4 queries and harms 9-12.
phases.decision: FAILURE. The policy is dominated. The result reframes the whole track: disagreement is not escalation value.

phases.name: Mechanism Analysis
phases.objective: Why does escalation help or hurt, and can the cases be told apart before paying?
phases.hypothesis: Helps come from BM25-held evidence Dense missed; harms from fusion corrupting correct Dense results.
phases.experiment: Per-query decomposition of all helps and harms into three states, with a bounded separation check over six pre-declared features.
phases.result: The hypothesis is confirmed as a mechanism (helps = State 2 BM25-rescue; harms = State 3, via intruder promotion or re-ranking among shared docs) but not separable in advance (1/6 and 0/6); only 5 unique positives.
phases.decision: Outcome B. No candidate promoted, no intervention run; the 'enough development examples' gate failed a priori and was honoured.

phases.name: Research Boundary
phases.objective: What can AdaptiveRAG legitimately conclude, and should it keep going?
phases.hypothesis: n/a (a boundary assessment, not an experiment).
phases.experiment: Audit of Gates 2/3/9 and Phases 10-11 against a go/no-go framework.
phases.result: Five independent failures agree (no pre-routing signal, chance DDR, no separation, few positives, net-negative rung).
phases.decision: STOP CURRENT ADAPTIVE-ROUTING TRACK (Position C), with re-entry conditions written down (dozens of positives + power analysis, an EV-positive rung, a pre-registered rule, split discipline, a gate that can say 'no').

phases.name: Next Direction (selection recorded)
phases.objective: Which alternative track, if any, is worth opening?
phases.hypothesis: A decision point before the embedding call could work where the post-dense one did not.
phases.experiment: Read-only counts over frozen rows (no retrieval, no fitting).
phases.result: The BM25 to Dense rung is EV-positive (+0.11 to +0.14 R@5) with 16/21 cheap-first positives and 91/86 queries needing no Dense call - 4-5x the headroom of any earlier framing, at a genuinely avoidable cost.

phases.name: Cheap-First Experiment
phases.objective: Can decision-time pre-Dense information predict when Dense is worth buying?
phases.hypothesis: A pre-registered low-dimensional rule over query + BM25 state matches dense-only quality at far fewer calls.
phases.experiment: Six allowlisted pre-Dense signals; frozen oracle; calibration rule freeze; one-pass test with random ablation.
phases.result: The rule bm25_slope >= -0.915 improves over BM25-only (+0.078 / +0.050) and beats random on one arm (P = 0.029) but not the other; it trails dense-only by 0.081/0.086 and catches only 5/11 positives; the success criterion fails outright.
phases.decision: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE. The open question (power vs noise) is named, and the sequel is a powered test, not a re-sweep.

phases.name: Powered Confirmation
phases.objective: Does the Phase 14 selection claim replicate with far more positives?
phases.hypothesis: The frozen rule selects Dense calls better than random and approaches dense-only quality.
phases.experiment: The rule applied unchanged to 110 fresh queries per arm (duplicate-screened, all test split), with bootstrap CIs, Holm within each comparison pair, and random-at-rate nulls.
phases.result: 18/25 positives caught at ~30% spend; beats random (P = 0.008 / 0.019, combined 0.001); +0.058/+0.045 over BM25 with CIs excluding zero; but -0.030 / -0.018 vs dense-only, missing the 0.02 bar by 0.004. Verdict: 4 of 5 success bars, no failure bar.
phases.decision: STOP. Two consecutive inconclusive phases with the same signature; the remaining question is a margin judgment, not a measurement gap.
